title: Mathlib Import
content: The proof imports the full Mathlib. The single arithmetic ingredient it actually relies on is `Int.gcd_eq_gcd_ab` (Bézout's identity) together with the cofactor function `Int.gcdA`; the rest is integer modular congruence (`Int.ModEq`) and coprimality (`IsCoprime.mul_dvd`).
mathContext: Bézout's identity `(Int.gcd a b : ℤ) = a * Int.gcdA a b + b * Int.gcdB a b` provides the modular inverse used at every Garner step, so no `ZMod.inv` machinery is needed.

title: Garner's Algorithm: The Open Question
content: The module documents the open question — extend the two-modulus solver `crtInt` to k pairwise-coprime moduli — and describes Garner's mixed-radix reconstruction: a single left-to-right sweep that carries only the running value `x` and the running partial product `P`. At step j the digit is `vⱼ = (rⱼ − x)·(P⁻¹ mod mⱼ)` reduced into `[0, mⱼ)`, after which `x ← x + vⱼ·P` and `P ← P·mⱼ`.
mathContext: Mixed-radix form: `x = v₁ + v₂·m₁ + v₃·m₁m₂ + ⋯ + v_k·m₁⋯m_{k-1}`. The `% m` reduction of each digit is exactly what bounds the running value into `[0, ∏ mᵢ)` — the defining feature of *Garner's* form versus a raw CRT sum.

title: digit: The Garner Digit
content: `digit x P m r = ((r - x) * Int.gcdA P m) % m` is the mixed-radix digit at the current step. It uses the Bézout cofactor `Int.gcdA P m` as the modular inverse of the partial product `P` modulo `m`, then reduces into `[0, m)` with `% m`.
mathContext: Since `P · gcdA P m ≡ 1 [ZMOD m]` whenever `gcd(P, m) = 1`, the digit equals `(r − x)·P⁻¹ mod m`, exactly the coefficient that corrects the running value to the residue `r` modulo `m`.

title: garnerAux and garner: The Sweep
content: `garnerAux` is the recursive accumulator: from `(x, P)` it processes `(m, r) :: rest` by recursing on `(x + digit·P, P·m)`. The public `garner pairs` sweeps from `(0, 1)` and returns the running value. The whole reconstruction is a single linear pass carrying just two integers.
mathContext: Updating `P ← P·m` keeps `P = m₁⋯m_{j-1}` as the partial product, so `digit·P` adds the next mixed-radix term without recomputing any inverse against the full modulus.

title: Digit Facts: Bounds and Congruence
content: `digit_nonneg` and `digit_lt` establish `0 ≤ digit < m` for `m > 0` directly from the Euclidean remainder bounds. `digit_modEq` records that the reduced digit is congruent to its un-reduced Bézout form `(r − x)·gcdA P m` modulo `m`, so the `% m` reduction drops out of all congruence reasoning.
mathContext: The bounds `0 ≤ x % m < m` are what make every mixed-radix digit genuinely a digit in base `m`; this is the source of the range bound `0 ≤ garner < ∏ mᵢ`.

title: garnerAux_snd: The Running Product
content: After the sweep the second accumulator component equals the starting `P` times the product of all moduli: `(garnerAux x P pairs).2 = P · (pairs.map fst).prod`. Starting from `P = 1`, this pins the mixed-radix modulus to `∏ mᵢ`, the CRT modulus.
mathContext: A straightforward induction with `ring`; this bookkeeping lemma is what lets the range and uniqueness theorems speak about `∏ mᵢ` rather than the opaque accumulator.

title: Modular Inverse from Bézout
content: `gcdA_mul_modEq_one` is the single arithmetic fact the whole development rests on: when `IsCoprime P m`, the Bézout cofactor satisfies `P · Int.gcdA P m ≡ 1 [ZMOD m]`. `isCoprime_list_prod_right` lifts coprimality with each list element to coprimality with the list product — needed to maintain coprimality of the partial product against the remaining moduli.
mathContext: From `gcd(P,m)=1` and `1 = P·gcdA + m·gcdB`, divisibility `m ∣ 1 − P·gcdA` gives `P·gcdA ≡ 1 [ZMOD m]`. This is the exact identity behind the parent `crtInt`, reused unchanged at every Garner step.

title: garnerAux_modEq_self: Residue Preservation
content: After processing the remaining pairs starting from `(x, P)`, the result is still `≡ x [ZMOD P]`. Because every modulus already solved divides the partial product `P`, this invariant is precisely what protects the residues of all earlier moduli from being disturbed by later steps.
mathContext: Each subsequent increment `digit·P` is a multiple of `P`, and the recursive product `P·m` is divisible by `P`, so the running value stays fixed modulo `P` throughout the rest of the sweep.

title: garnerAux_modEq: Every Congruence Holds
content: The swept value satisfies `value ≡ p.2 [ZMOD p.1]` for every pair `p`. The head congruence is solved because `x + digit·P ≡ x + (r − x) = r [ZMOD m]` (using the Bézout inverse), and the preservation lemma carries this through the rest of the sweep. Tail congruences follow directly by induction.
mathContext: Head step: `digit·P ≡ (r − x)·(P·gcdA P m) ≡ (r − x)·1 = r − x [ZMOD m]`, then `garnerAux_modEq_self` fixes the value modulo `m` (since `m ∣ P·m`) for all later steps.

title: garnerAux_range: The Mixed-Radix Bound
content: By induction maintaining `0 ≤ x < P`, and using `0 ≤ digit < m`, the new value `x + digit·P` stays in `[0, P·m)`. This yields the genuine mixed-radix bound `0 ≤ garner < ∏ mᵢ`, distinguishing Garner's form from an unbounded CRT sum.
mathContext: The arithmetic core is `x + (m−1)·P + P = P·m`: with `x < P` and `digit ≤ m − 1`, we get `x + digit·P < P·m`. Closed with `linarith` after `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right`.

title: Public Interface: Correct, Bounded, Unique
content: `garner_modEq` (every congruence solved), `garner_range` (canonical representative in `[0, ∏ mᵢ)`), and `garner_unique` (any in-range solution equals `garner`) together state that Garner returns *the* CRT solution. Uniqueness lifts each `mᵢ ∣ (garner − y)` to `∏ mᵢ ∣ (garner − y)` via pairwise coprimality, then forces the quotient `c` to satisfy `|c| < 1`, hence `c = 0`.
mathContext: Two representatives of the same residue class lying in `[0, ∏ mᵢ)` differ by a multiple of `∏ mᵢ` strictly smaller in magnitude than `∏ mᵢ`, so they coincide — the standard CRT uniqueness argument, here driven by `IsCoprime.mul_dvd` and `isCoprime_list_prod_right`.
